added_paragraph: **Latitude under continuing severe need, 6 October 2026:** the [ethical-minimum continuation](theories/shengsheng-buxi-generative-existence/unified-2026-10-05/UNIVERSAL-ETHICAL-MINIMUM.md#a-restricted-permission-while-serious-need-remains) defends a restricted permission through two explicit disputed judgments: the helper's complete irreversible loss is graver than each patient's complete bounded loss, and separate weaker claims do not solely by their number require its sacrifice. [Argument, sources and review](_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-INTEGRATION.md) require symmetric patient histories and preserve independently required compatible rescue. Equal goods alone do not transport permission across different practical situations. Next is testing the aggregation premise against serious competing claims; no general latitude against a stronger individual claim or universal grounding is established. The full goal remains active.

**A restricted latitude candidate, 6 October 2026:** [the current minimum](unified-2026-10-05/UNIVERSAL-ETHICAL-MINIMUM.md#a-restricted-permission-while-serious-need-remains) now confronts actual unmet severe need while defending protection of a substantially graver complete individual loss. Its restriction on combining weaker claims is substantive and disputed. The account counts each patient's history as fully as the helper's, preserves compatible bounded rescue, and distinguishes shared value from transferable permission. The next bridge tests how serious claims may combine; general personal latitude and the universal foundation remain unfinished.

**Latitude under actual continuing need, 6 October 2026:** read the [restricted permission argument](LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-ARGUMENT.md), [demanding counterreview](LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-REVIEW.md), [primary arguments](LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-SOURCES.md), [permission-transport test](LATITUDE-PERMISSION-TRANSPORT.md), and [integration](LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-INTEGRATION.md). The candidate exposes its complete-loss comparison and restriction on combining weaker claims. Patient histories cannot be fragmented, and protection of a project does not erase independently required compatible relief. The full goal remains active; next is a direct serious-claims aggregation test.

**Bounded duty → restricted latitude under real need, 6 October 2026:** [the new ethical comparison](UNIVERSAL-ETHICAL-MINIMUM.md#a-restricted-permission-while-serious-need-remains) defends a narrow permission using an explicit ranking of each person's complete loss and a disputed restriction on combining separate weaker claims. Both are supplied ethical judgments under argument; generative differentiation and equal standing do not entail them. The study requires symmetric historical accounting, preserves bounded rescue compatible with the same protected goods, and prevents permission transport across changed responsibilities or capacities. Actual noncompliance remains in the case, and hypothetical provision does not relieve patients. Next is testing the aggregation principle against serious claims; stronger individual conflicts and deeper patient-to-actor grounding remain open. Existing conditional completion and the full universal-minimum objective retain their scopes.

Recorded 6 October 2026: [the latitude source study](../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/LATITUDE-UNDER-NEED-SOURCES.md) directly inspects two Scheffler texts and Murphy's 1993 argument; the [permission-transport study](../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/LATITUDE-PERMISSION-TRANSPORT.md) adds selected Cullity 2009 manuscript passages. Exact access scopes, primary URLs and temporary byte hashes are recorded; no source PDFs are imported. The normative construction is AI-authored and is not attributed to those authors. The [pre-latitude canonical snapshot metadata](../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/development/UNIVERSAL-ETHICAL-MINIMUM-BEFORE-LATITUDE.json) preserves its original bytes and link base.
